site_ui.lead: Probate practitioners converge on one hard rule, that nothing moves on an estate property until the court issues letters, and this volume maps every step from petition and letters through court confirmation, heir decisions, and the specialist business built around them.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies from realtors, estate attorneys, and probate software operators, with timestamped inline attribution on every quote, metric, pro-tip, and operator gate. Coverage runs from filing and letters through court confirmation and overbids, inherited-house decisions, cleanouts, agent listing playbooks, attorney referrals, lead data, calling, wholesaling, and senior transitions.

flow: File in the decedent's county of domicile with the original will, certified death certificate, petition and fee, listing every heir and relative, including disinherited ones.
Notify heirs and publish, have a non-party mail the DE121 notice with proof filed, and clear the hearing.
Request full IAEA authority, order at least 5 to 10 certified copies of letters, and treat the letters date as the earliest listing date.
Obtain an EIN, run all estate money through a dedicated estate account, and pay debts in statutory priority order.
Order a preliminary title report as soon as full-authority letters issue, and confirm every heir and heir's spouse can sign before any contract.

Full-authority sales close in 18 to 30 days like regular listings. Limited-authority sales go to a confirmation hearing, where overbids open at the price plus 10 percent of the first $10,000 and 5 percent of the balance.
